title: P0 multiplex scheduler queueing surge retrospective
summary: On 2028-11-21 at ~03:14 UTC Redwood experienced a P0 outage affecting hosted API streaming sessions. A sudden, high-cardinality surge from a single large customer triggered an interaction between the multiplexing scheduler and the session KV cache that resulted in head-of-line queueing, streaming fragmentation, and an elevated 5xx rate for roughly 14 minutes. The incident caused degraded tail latency and partial failure of streaming responses for ~12% of requests from impacted shards.
impact:
- Duration: 03:14 UTC to 03:28 UTC (mitigations started 03:18, full recovery by 03:28).
- Affected surface: hosted API streaming endpoints in us-west and us-east regions, ~7% of total streaming requests globally during the window (peak concurrency ~18k multiplexed sessions on affected hosts).
- Symptoms: visible client disconnects and stream reconnections, increased streaming fragmentation (chunks split across reconnects), 5xx increase from baseline 0.03% to 2.4% at peak, p95 latency from 240ms -> 3.2s for streaming handshake and first chunk.
timeline:
2028-11-21 03:13 UTC - Gradual rise in multiplexed session attempts from a large customer (background load test)
2028-11-21 03:14 UTC - Alerts: streaming error rate alert fires; on-call paged
2028-11-21 03:15 UTC - Engineers confirm elevated 5xx and reconnects; initial hypothesis: network flaps or edge TLS
2028-11-21 03:16 UTC - Dashboard shows heavy queue depth on multiplex scheduler worker process; KV cache miss latency also increases
2028-11-21 03:17 UTC - Attempted mitigation: increase per-worker multiplex slot limit via dynamic config (rolled to 10% of hosts) — no immediate improvement
2028-11-21 03:18 UTC - Applied targeted routing: move new streams to cold pool (reduced new session acceptance) — visible reduction in new errors
2028-11-21 03:22 UTC - Identified root cause signal: scheduler backpressure + synchronous KV cache locking causing head-of-line blocking
2028-11-21 03:24 UTC - Hotfix: disable strict slot coalescing in scheduler and enable optimistic session de-duplication; 5xx trend declines
2028-11-21 03:28 UTC - Error rate returns to baseline, metrics stabilize; incident declared mitigated
root_cause: A combination of factors created a tight failure mode: (1) A sudden burst of highly concurrent streaming session requests that targeted the same set of multiplexing worker shards; (2) the scheduler's aggressive coalescing optimization attempted to pack many logical streams into limited multiplex slots and performed synchronous session-key checks against the central KV cache; (3) KV cache lock contention and elevated RPC latency caused scheduler goroutines to block, which produced head-of-line blocking on the multiplex connection causing streaming fragments to be delayed and client timeouts to surface as 5xx. Secondary contributor: the autoscaler decision window reacted poorly to the rapid burst and performed partial scale-down/scale-up cycles (thrash) that amplified the instability for ~90s.
detection_and_response:
Detection: standard error-rate and streaming fragmentation alerts triggered. First human response within 2 minutes. Initial triage focused on network/edge because reconnects matched previous TLS-rehandshake incidents, but metric correlation (multiplex queue depth, KV cache RPC latency) quickly shifted root-cause hypothesis.
Response: on-call SREs throttled new session routing to cold pool, toggled scheduler coalescing config, and applied optimistic de-duplication to avoid sync KV lookups. Runtime engineers deployed a lightweight fix to change the KV session lookup from a blocking lock to a lock-free fast-path for hot keys. These combined mitigations removed the blocking pressure and allowed hosts to drain queued streams.
Communications: status page updated at 03:20 UTC. Customer success notified high-volume customers by 03:30 UTC with mitigation summary.
immediate_mitigations:
- Throttled onboarding of new streaming sessions to cold pool (re-route rule)
- Disabled strict slot coalescing in multiplex scheduler (config toggle)
- Enabled optimistic session de-duplication to avoid synchronous KV checks
- Increased autoscaler cooldown to 180s and temporarily suspended aggressive scale-down policies for affected worker pools
- Rolled a runtime patch that exposes a lock-free KV fast-path for session canonicalization
long_term_actions:
- (Priority P0) Replace synchronous KV session-lock path with a fully lock-free session canonicalizer across all regions (ENG-runtime, owner: Ravi Patel) — target: 2 sprints
- Harden scheduler coalescing heuristics: add request-distribution awareness and hot-key detection to avoid packing high-cardinality bursts onto single shards (ENG-runtime, owner: Jon Chen) — target: 3 sprints
- Autoscaler tuning: implement burst-aware adapters and a fast-path for forced emergency scale-up to avoid thrash (ENG-platform, owner: Marta Kline) — target: 4 sprints
- Add synthetic tests that emulate high-cardinality multiplex bursts and verify no head-of-line blocking (SRE + QA, owner: Ewa Nowak) — target: next on-call rotation
- Create runbook entries for rapid detection of KV lock contention and recommended temporary mitigations (on-call SRE playbook) — target: 1 week
postmortem_actions:
- Create dashboard tile that surfaces per-worker multiplex queue depth, KV lock hold times, and per-key hotness (owner: Ravi)
- Land the lock-free session canonicalizer PR and measure tail latencies in canary cluster (owner: Ravi)
- Update alerting: add an aggregate metric combining queue_depth * kv_rpc_latency to triage faster (owner: Jon)
- Run tabletop exercise simulating similar burst from a single tenant and validate runbook effectiveness (owner: Ewa)
- Document customer communication template for rapid incident updates specific to streaming fragmentation (owner: CS lead)
retrospective_notes:
- The initial triage tunnelled on edge/TLS due to symptom similarity; ensure future triage checks include multiplex queue depth and KV latency as first-class signals for streaming issues.
- Config toggles (coalescing, optimistic dedupe) worked well as short-term mitigations but underline need for safer defaults.
- Autoscaler behavior needs a burst-mode policy to avoid taking actions in response to transient telemetry spikes.
- Action items are prioritized; agree to bi-weekly progress check-ins until all P0 items completed.
- Consider customer-facing postmortem for the largest impacted tenant if requested by CS.
notes_to_oncall:
If you see similar symptoms:
1) Check multiplex_worker_queue_depth and kv_cache_rpc_p50/p95 immediately.
2) If queue_depth > threshold AND kv_rpc_p95 > 200ms: toggle scheduler.coalesce=false and enable optimistic_session_dedupe.
3) Route new streams to cold-pool for 10 minutes and notify platform to hold aggressive scale-down.
4) Escalate to runtime owner (Ravi) and autoscaler owner (Marta) if no improvement in 2 minutes.
Include these steps in the runbook and pin to the streaming alert runbook.
